But the finding changes no decision, because the rule it calls obsolete had already been superseded before round 20. (1) CONTEXT 27 Sep 11:09:39Z, the user's letter (b): V*_C -> {V*_C, #37 56563521}, and #38 leaves. (2) CONTEXT 18:50Z, READ TABLE v2 item (9): 'V_pub >= 0.955 and non-CI -> {V_pub, #37}; #38 leaves ... The partner is always #37.' So the proposed action ('propose {F1, #37}, mark R14-RC-C superseded') is already the standing rule; the extra cap 8/12 clause is covered by 'the partner is always #37'. The quantitative claim is also unsupported. It sizes y from the lab (|y| 0.0003-0.0006; ins_cap6.json -0.00079/-0.00052, in-sample) and x from the public LB. Probe 45 falsified that lab sign, and the public LB puts y in (0.001, 0.003), at least as large as x in (0, 0.002). With comparable magnitudes, P(x<0) 0.10-0.20 and P(y<0) now below the lab-based 0.35-0.5, E[diff] at cap 6 is +/-1e-4 with no resolved sign. 'As F1's cap rises #37 dominates' ignores that a higher public read at cap 8/12 also lowers P(y<0). The objective is also medal rank, not E[score]. So this is a redundant re-derivation with an overstated magnitude claim, not a new finding.
